title: Flawed Type Guards and Discriminated Union Bypass
platform_conditions: Type-checker behavior only; the guard body is plain JavaScript at runtime wherever the compiled output runs
security_mechanism: A user-defined type guard ('x is Admin') is trusted unconditionally by the checker: whatever the body returns becomes the compiler's truth, so a guard that returns true (or tests a field the attacker controls) makes every later access type-correct at compile time and arbitrary at runtime. Discriminated unions have the same failure when the discriminant field (kind/type/role) comes from the payload: the attacker picks the variant, and narrowing selects the privileged branch of a switch written for internal values. Spread of an attacker object into a typed target also carries extra properties silently (excess property checks do not apply to spreads), performing batch assignment under a narrow type.

source_sink_clues.source: Request payloads and decoded JSON whose shape is decided by the client, then narrowed by guards or discriminant fields.
source_sink_clues.sink: 'x is T' guard functions with permissive bodies; switch/match on payload-supplied discriminants gating privileged branches; spread of attacker objects into strongly-typed targets

tracking_guards: Check each type guard body actually validates the fields it asserts (typeof/=== per member), check discriminant values are validated against a fixed set before narrowing drives privilege decisions, and check target objects are built field-by-field from validated input instead of spread.
not_candidate_when: The guard performs full field-level validation, the discriminant is computed server-side from validated data, or the narrowed branch is non-privileged and cannot affect authorization state.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: function isAdmin(x: any): x is Admin { return true; }
synthetic_safe_example: function isAdmin(x: any): x is Admin { return x && x.role === 'admin'; }
public_references: CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html
